name: Procedural Generation: Rules Build Worlds
truth: A generated world carries choices about representation, growth, connection and support. Those choices can be inspected and revised.
qfep_connection: Investigate how local rules, sampled fields and authored constraints make forms and routes possible. Entropy claims require a stated measure; appearance alone does not establish a threshold.
description: Build on arrays, fields, cellular updates and grammars: select a form, guide and branch growth, test connections, construct interiors, sample material and compose networks.
learning_objectives: Compare a represented body with the criterion used to select it
Read target assignment and vector accumulation as an explicit growth decision
Distinguish a strand, a branching tree and a connected network
Construct and test interior passage for a declared body
Track what survives when simulation is sampled, cut or repeated
content: PG_Genetic_Evolution: Primitive descriptions, incomplete volume estimates and selection; held witness and independent floor support
PG_Space_Colonization: Assign targets, sum unit directions, compare tips with persistent growth sites; held witness and explicit support
PG_Branching_Growth: Nearest-target growth, repeated positions, held geometry and explicit variation
PG_Percolation_Network: Face contact, finite lattice reachability and the distinction between flow and collision
PG_Caves_Mazes: Biased carving centres, maze backtracking, headroom and independent museum support
PG_Sculpted_Forms: Physical cubes, centre-based voxel sampling, Boolean cutting and layered surfaces
PG_Mirrored_Patterns: Held cellular fields, copying operations, distinct graph edges and surface construction

artifact_groups.rationale: Six-body controlled comparison using the existing genetic kernel. Change target, expose an uncounted ring, preserve a witness and inspect one generation; original grid screen retained as secondary.
Heavy compute solo map: trees grow toward attractors via space colonization. Branching structure emerges from point-cloud competition — growth without blueprint.
Two growth strategies compared: branching algorithm builds tree-like structures toward attractors, organic noise space sculpts terrain from Perlin fields. Medium compute, safe to pair.
artifact_groups.description: Nearest-target growth, repeated positions, held geometry and explicit variation

artifact_groups.rationale: Heavy compute solo map: percolation network CA tests connectivity thresholds in random grids. Dark sphere anchors the visual field as clusters form or fragment at the critical probability.
artifact_groups.description: Face contact, finite lattice reachability and the distinction between flow and collision

artifact_groups.rationale: Procedural exploration spaces: cave random walk carves tunnels through solid rock, maze generation builds corridors from recursive backtracking. Two strategies for explorable worlds.
artifact_groups.description: Biased carving centres, maze backtracking, headroom and independent museum support

artifact_groups.rationale: Geometric construction: cube mound accumulates voxels, dome subdivides icosahedra, layered membrane stacks transparent surfaces. Three ways rules sculpt form from accumulation.
artifact_groups.description: Physical cubes, centre-based voxel sampling, Boolean cutting and layered surfaces

artifact_groups.rationale: Pattern from reflection and branching: mirrored cellular texture wraps CA output symmetrically onto 3D form, rhizomatic maze builds non-hierarchical branching networks. Light compute synthesis.
